title: Image Quality Assessment for Embodied AI
claim: Different visual systems fail under different distortions, and agents with downstream decision and execution steps need a dedicated perception quality indicator.
layout: 3 stacked rows: two top panels, pipeline strip, three bottom panels; arrows left-to-right
description: A dense, colorful multi-panel figure. The top row has a blue 'Human Visual System' panel and a green 'Machine Visual System' panel. Each pairs a noisy photo or saliency heatmap with text on how perception and cognition are affected. Cartoon icons of a person and a computer sit beside them. Below, an orange 'Robot Visual System' band shows a left-to-right pipeline of Perception, Cognition, Decision and Execution. Each stage has an icon, big blue arrows, and human-vs-robot analogues (eye/camera, cerebrum/VLM, cerebellum/VLA, arm/motor). Robot-scene photos are shown at each stage. The bottom row has three panels. Two show reference vs. distorted image pairs with task failure explanations (Cognition vs Decision, Decision vs Execution). The third is a diagram with an 'Embodied IQA' box that evaluates how distortion affects each stage. The eye goes first to the colored panel headers and the central robot pipeline.
caption: The significant gap between human, machine, and robot visual systems. Humans and Machines are sensitive to different distortions, while Robots have Decision and Execution steps beyond Cognition, highlighting the importance of a Perception quality index for Embodied AI.
abstract: Embodied AI has developed rapidly in recent years, but it is still mainly deployed in laboratories, with various distortions in the Real-world limiting its application. Traditionally, Image Quality Assessment (IQA) methods are applied to predict human preferences for distorted images; however, there is no IQA method to assess the usability of an image in embodied tasks, namely, the perceptual quality for robots. To provide accurate and reliable quality indicators for future embodied scenarios, we first propose the topic: IQA for Embodied AI. Specifically, we (1) based on the Mertonian system and meta-cognitive theory, constructed a perception-cognition-decision-execution pipeline and defined a comprehensive subjective score collection process; (2) established the Embodied-IQA database, containing over 36k reference/distorted image pairs, with more than 5m fine-grained annotations provided by Vision Language Models/Vision Language Action-models/Real-world robots; (3) trained and validated the performance of mainstream IQA methods on Embodied-IQA, demonstrating the need to develop more accurate quality indicators for Embodied AI. We sincerely hope that through evaluation, we can promote the application of Embodied AI under complex distortions in the Real-world. Project page: https://github.com/lcysyzxdxc/EmbodiedIQA
